worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{(x-2)(x-3)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{B}{x-3}+\frac{C}{(x-3)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)(x-3)^{2}$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}=A(x-3)^{2}+B(x-3)(x-2)+C(x-2).
$$

Plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(3)^{2} & =A(3-3)^{2}+B(3-3)(3-2)+C(3-2) \\ 9 & =C \\ C & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$  we can eliminate  $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(2)^{2} & =A(2-3)^{2}+B(2-3)(2-2)+C(2-2) \\ 4 & =A \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $A$ and $C,$ we can solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0)^{2} & =A(0-3)^{2}+B(0-3)(0-2)+C(0-2) \\ 0 & =9A+6B-2C \\ 0 & =9(4)+6B-2(9) \\ 0 & =18+6B \\ -6B & =18 \\ B & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{(x-2)(x-3)^{2}}=\frac{4}{x-2}-\frac{3}{x-3}+\frac{9}{(x-3)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{(x-2)(x-3)^{2}}\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{4}{x-2}-\frac{3}{x-3}+\frac{9}{(x-3)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =4\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x+9\int \frac{1}{(x-3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|-\frac{9}{x-3}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
